playbook:
When I am dealt K and I act first, I bet to extract value and apply pressure.
When I am dealt K and my opponent checks to me, I bet for value rather than giving a free showdown.
When my opponent bets and I hold K, I continue (call) to contest a single-unit bet — do not fold a King to small bets.
When I am dealt Q and I act first, I usually open with a bet to take the initiative and get value.
When I am dealt Q and my opponent checks to me, I usually bet to steal or build value; I will mix in occasional checks to avoid being exploitable.
When my opponent bets and I hold Q, I call modest single-unit bets to contest the pot and extract value; fold only to very large bets or strong pattern evidence of no bluffs.
When I am dealt J and I act first, I check (do not bluff too often from the worst card).
When my opponent bets and I hold J, I generally call small single-unit bets to keep the pot contested given the deck odds; fold if pot odds or opponent behavior make calling clearly unprofitable.
When I am behind in match equity (chip deficit), shift to more aggression: bet K consistently and increase betting frequency with Q to apply pressure and try to recover chips; still avoid over-bluffing with J.
When I am ahead in match equity, favor straightforward value betting with K and Q and avoid unnecessary bluffs with J.
Introduce occasional, rare deviations (check some K or bet some J very infrequently) to remain unpredictable, but keep those deviations rare and deliberate.
At showdown always declare my actual card truthfully.
